slot.brief: Show a substrate structure in a figure; ask which reagent (Lucas reagent sequence) distinguishes the given alcohols by rate/appearance.

stem: Which reagent distinguishes the alcohol shown in the figure from a primary alcohol by the rapid appearance of turbidity at room temperature?

verdicts.working: Figure shows (CH3)3C–OH (tertiary alcohol). Lucas reagent = conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2. Tertiary alcohols form a stable 3° carbocation (SN1) and give insoluble alkyl chloride as immediate turbidity at room temperature; primary alcohols show no turbidity. Only option A is the Lucas reagent.

working:
The compound shown in the figure is 2-methylpropan-2-ol ($tert$-butanol), which is a tertiary ($3^\circ$) alcohol. Lucas reagent is an equimolar mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$. Tertiary alcohols react via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism involving a stable tertiary carbocation intermediate, reacting almost instantaneously to produce an insoluble alkyl chloride: $$\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. } \text{ZnCl}_2} \text{(CH}_3)_3\text{C-Cl}\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$ This insoluble alkyl chloride appears immediately as turbidity or cloudiness. In contrast, primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature under these conditions.

Independent check: Figure shows (CH3)3C–OH (tertiary alcohol). Lucas reagent = conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2. Tertiary alcohols form a stable 3° carbocation (SN1) and give insoluble alkyl chloride as immediate turbidity at room temperature; primary alcohols show no turbidity. Only option A is the Lucas reagent.

draft.distractor_notes:
Dilute HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2 incorrectly uses dilute acid, which provides insufficient hydronium and chloride activity to drive the conversion.
Conc. HCl + anhydrous AlCl3 confuses the Lucas reagent Lewis acid (ZnCl2) with the Lewis acid typically used in Friedel–Crafts alkylation/acylation.
Conc. H2SO4 + anhydrous ZnCl2 replaces hydrochloric acid with sulfuric acid, which lacks nucleophilic chloride ions and promotes alcohol dehydration rather than alkyl chloride precipitation.

figure.description: Skeletal structure of 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butyl alcohol). A central carbon atom is bonded to three methyl groups (-CH3) and one hydroxyl group (-OH).
